rationale: The per-round receipt (CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849) settled the persistence question with no comparison gaps: the control round without a forgery grants nothing (index 29), each of the three forged rounds grants the same retried pre-vote (indices 32, 35, 38), and the two repair comparisons hold (indices 33 and 36: the leader's heartbeat restores lead from 0 to 1 after each forgery). So the window is not a single heartbeat interval that a one-off message opens: a sender that repeats the message each round keeps the follower's lease suppression off while the leader is healthy and still beating, and the failure is the sender's cadence rather than a broken repair path. I record that as a Fact, write the child-level account, and revise the parent account so its limitation list no longer says the repeated-message case is unexecuted; the joint history now covers four receipts of the same lineage.

knowledge.statement: Repeating the peer-form MsgForgetLeader once per heartbeat round keeps a follower from enforcing the leader lease: over three consecutive rounds the leader's real heartbeat restored the follower's leader context (lead 0 -> 1) and the accepted message cleared it again (1 -> 0), and the identical retried pre-vote from an up-to-date candidate was granted in every round, while the leader remained StateLeader at term 2 throughout.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 29, 32, 33, 35, 36 and 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, voters {1,2,3} from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1; only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire; the candidate's pre-vote request is reused unchanged as a retry and its grant is not fed back.

interpretations.rationale: The persistence question is answered yes, and the wiring revision is what made it answerable: each round now has its own admission event, so all six comparisons completed. Control: the round without a forged message granted nothing and produced no response at all (index 29), so withholding under the lease is real and not an artefact of the candidate. Persistence: the accepted message cleared the leader context and the identical retried pre-vote was granted in round 1 (index 32), round 2 (index 35) and round 3 (index 38) - three independent witnesses, each with its own admission event. Repair: the two comparisons that matter for attribution hold (indices 33 and 36), i.e. after each forgery the leader's real heartbeat restored lead from 0 to 1, so the repeated success of the forgery is the sender's cadence defeating a working repair rather than a broken repair path. The leader stayed StateLeader at term 2 for the whole loop (index 39, an uncited observation), so the follower's support was withdrawn while the leader was demonstrably alive. Combined with the parent question's account, the disruption is not limited to one heartbeat interval: a sender can hold the lease suppression off for as long as it keeps sending, which makes every retry of an up-to-date candidate's pre-vote (and, from the quorum receipt, its vote) succeed.
counterevidence: The leading competing explanation for the grants - that this follower grants pre-votes to any up-to-date candidate regardless of its leader - is excluded by the control round in this same receipt (index 29) and in every earlier receipt.
The repair path is not broken and the effect is not monotonic degradation: lead returns to 1 in every round that was preceded by a forgery (indices 33 and 36).
limitations: Three rounds in one process with hand-delivered messages; the cadence is exact (one message per heartbeat tick) and no jitter, loss or reordering is exercised.
The candidate's request is reused unchanged and its grants are not fed back, so this measures the follower's answers rather than a completed election.
The follower is alone in the loop; the quorum-scale version is covered by the earlier receipt, not re-measured here.

interpretations.rationale: Current account of the question across all four receipts. A MsgForgetLeader sent by a peer in wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) is accepted through RawNode.Step with no error and clears the follower's live leader context (Lead 1 -> 0): witnessed at index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 and reproduced at index 22 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a. It changes the support the follower gives an up-to-date candidate: the identical pre-vote that produced no response under the lease is granted after the accepted message (controls hold in every receipt), the follower then grants the real vote, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent still reports StateLeader at term 2 (indices 14, 15, 17 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; index 25 of the latest). The window opened per message is closed by the next genuine leader message - the leader's next heartbeat restored lead=1 after one leader tick and the same pre-vote was ignored again (indices 7, 8 of the same receipt) - but a sender that repeats the message each round keeps the suppression off without any failure of that repair: three consecutive rounds each restored the context and each was defeated again, with the retried pre-vote granted every time (indices 32, 35, 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849, whose repair comparisons hold at 33 and 36). The harm remains bounded: the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append, becomes a follower at term 3 following it, and the anchor equals the committed prefix it already had (index 26 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a), so this is a forced, unnecessary leadership change with no committed-entry loss. Cause and controls are unchanged: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg although only the local ForgetLeader APIs produce it, and because the wire form has no term field Step treats it as a local message and skips all term checks; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected with ErrStepLocalMsg in every receipt. Remaining limits are scope, not severity: single process, hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refuses the message outright, and the incumbent is only observed through the first new-leader append.
interpretations.joint_history: All four cited receipts are separate executions of one fixed-experiment lineage in the same package with the same construction (three real RawNode instances built from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1 with voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, a real election for node 1 and hand-delivered messages through the public Step path). CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 is the original harness; CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568 is its revised successor (previous_id = the original) that added the repair-path and quorum-stream scenarios; CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a is the successor that added the aftermath scenario with per-stream event names; CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849 is the successor that added the per-round persistence loop. Each run prints into its own runner stream and builds its own nodes, so no cited index depends on another run's bytes; where the same predicate is witnessed in several receipts it is because the harness re-executed the same scenario, never because observations were joined across runs.
counterevidence: The competing explanation that this follower grants pre-votes and votes regardless of its leader is excluded by the under-lease control in every receipt, including the freshly executed control round inside the persistence loop.
The change is per-message: in every round where the leader's heartbeat was processed, the context returned (lead 0 -> 1), so the defect is not a stuck state and does not survive a sender that stops.
The widest severity reading is excluded by the aftermath receipt: the deposed incumbent conceded and the new leader's log continued the committed prefix, so no committed entry was lost.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the documented inbound path, repeatedly; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test.

Single-process, hand-delivered messages: no wall-clock duration, jitter, packet loss or multi-host transport behaviour is measured, and the persistence loop used an exact one-message-per-tick cadence.
The follower-side effect is measured per node; the quorum-scale election was measured on one voter in the earlier receipt and not re-measured under the repeated cadence.
The incumbent is observed only through the first append from the new leader.
